claims.text: Brain imaging (CT or MRI, with or without angiography) to characterize the lesion: infarct, hemorrhage or mass.
claims.quote: Brain imaging (eg, CT, MRI; with or without angiographic protocols) is required to characterize the lesion (eg, infarct, hemorrhage, mass).

claims.text: Neuroimaging after a TIA too, because infarct, small hemorrhage or mass cannot be excluded clinically; CT may miss infarcts for > 24 hours.
claims.quote: Because an infarct, a small hemorrhage, and even a mass lesion cannot be excluded clinically, neuroimaging is required. Usually, CT is the study most likely to be immediately available. However, CT may not identify infarcts for > 24 hours.

claims.text: CT angiography, MRA or diffusion-weighted MRI of the carotid and cerebral circulation after every TIA.
claims.quote: All patients who have had a TIA require CT angiography, magnetic resonance angiography (MRA), or diffusion-weighted MRI of the carotid and cerebral circulation.

claims.text: Look for the source: carotid stenosis, cardiac emboli, atrial fibrillation, hematologic abnormalities and stroke risk factors.
claims.quote: evaluation includes tests for carotid stenosis, cardiac sources of emboli, atrial fibrillation, and hematologic abnormalities and screening for stroke risk factors.
